item.title: Taddeo Campaign Launches Ad Attacking Ingoglia's CFO Record
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democrat Annette Taddeo's campaign for Florida Chief Financial Officer rolled out a new digital ad Monday attacking Republican Blaise Ingoglia's tenure in the office, according to a press release from CVS Communications. The 30-second spot highlights recent scrutiny of the Department of Financial Services under Ingoglia's watch, including missing…
item.content:encoded:
Democrat Annette Taddeo's campaign for Florida Chief Financial Officer rolled out a new digital ad Monday attacking Republican Blaise Ingoglia's tenure in the office, according to a press release from CVS Communications. The 30-second spot highlights recent scrutiny of the Department of Financial Services under Ingoglia's watch, including missing documentation for more than $342 million in contracts and a grand jury's findings on a $10 million Hope Florida Medicaid settlement.

The ad accuses Ingoglia of giving insurance companies a $3 billion bailout and diverting $10 million meant for sick children toward political activity. "Ingoglia's corruption has gone wild, and it's costing you more," the narrator states, before Taddeo pledges to lower insurance rates and ensure accountability.

Taddeo, a South Florida business owner who founded LanguageSpeak three decades ago, flipped a Republican state Senate seat in 2017 to become the first Latina Democrat elected to the Florida Senate. She served five years on the Banking and Insurance Committee before launching her bid for the statewide financial oversight position, focusing on insurance costs, accountability, and protecting taxpayer dollars.

The closure affects all classes, campus activities, special events, and online instruction. The college is still evaluating when it will be safe to reopen and has not yet…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College announced Monday that all its locations will remain closed Tuesday, October 13, as the college continues to assess conditions before resuming operations.

The closure affects all classes, campus activities, special events, and online instruction. The college is still evaluating when it will be safe to reopen and has not yet announced a firm date for resuming normal operations.

Fall B session final exams and the start of the D session will be rescheduled once PSC determines when classes can resume. Students and staff are urged to monitor PSC's social media accounts, the college website at PensacolaState.edu, and PSC Alert for updates as the situation develops.

item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa Island Authority has canceled its committee meeting scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, according to a news release from the agency.

All items that were set for discussion during the committee meeting will instead be addressed at the SRIA's next full board meeting, scheduled for Wednesday, October 28. The authority, which oversees operations on Pensacola Beach, did not provide a reason for the cancellation.

Residents and those interested in SRIA business can find updated meeting information at sria-fla.com. The Santa Rosa Island Authority operates under the direction of Escambia County and receives its funding entirely from lease fees paid by businesses and residents on Pensacola Beach.

item.content:encoded: Santa Rosa County officials have rescinded evacuation orders for Zones A, B, and C, according to a county news release reported by WKRG News 5. The lifting of evacuation orders does not extend to Navarre Beach, which remains closed to residents and the public. The decision suggests improving conditions in the affected areas, though officials are maintaining restrictions on the beach community as a precautionary measure. Additional details about the timeline for Navarre Beach's reopening have not yet been announced.

item.title: Escambia County Schools Closed Tuesday for Storm Damage Repairs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Public Schools will remain closed Tuesday, October 13, as the district works to repair damage and restore essential services across its campuses, according to a Monday announcement from ECPS Communications. School officials say district personnel and contractors are actively addressing damage from what appears to be recent severe…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools will remain closed Tuesday, October 13, as the district works to repair damage and restore essential services across its campuses, according to a Monday announcement from ECPS Communications.

School officials say district personnel and contractors are actively addressing damage from what appears to be recent severe weather. The district is coordinating with local utility companies to restore power and other vital services to school buildings. Transportation teams are also assessing bus routes to ensure safe operations before resuming service.

"The safety of our students, their families, our employees and this community remains our top priority," the district said in a statement. ECPS said it will post further updates through its Focus Communications system, social media, and local media outlets as repairs continue.

item.title: ECMS Foundation Names 16 Finalists for 3rd Annual Health Excellence Awards
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Medical Society Foundation has announced the finalists for its third consecutive year of Health Excellence Awards, recognizing individuals and organizations improving health outcomes in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties. Sixteen finalists were selected from nominations submitted by colleagues, patients, and community members.…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Medical Society Foundation has announced the finalists for its third consecutive year of Health Excellence Awards, recognizing individuals and organizations improving health outcomes in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties.

Sixteen finalists were selected from nominations submitted by colleagues, patients, and community members. The winner announcement will take place Thursday, October 29 at 6:00 p.m. at the Jean & Paul Amos Performance Studio. According to the foundation, awards will be presented across seven categories that include both clinical and non-clinical roles, as well as honors for ECMS Physician Members.

"Every one of these finalists was nominated by someone who sees their work up close and wanted to make sure it was recognized," said Ellen W. McKnight, MD, president of the ECMS Foundation. The finalists represent a range of healthcare professionals and supporters working in the local medical community.

Tickets and sponsorships for the October 29 event are available at escambiacms.org/hea. The foundation notes that past years have sold out, and encourages early registration. Emerald Coast Hospice is returning as the Legacy Presenting Sponsor. Proceeds benefit the ECMS Foundation's community health programs, which include the Go Seniors! Transportation program, the Blood Pressure Cuff Program, and physician wellness initiatives, along with scholarships at FSU College of Medicine's Pensacola Regional Campus and Pensacola State College.

item.title: EREC Outages Drop Below 700 in Escambia as Restoration Efforts Continue

As of late Sunday night, EREC reported 678 outages remaining in Escambia County, down from higher numbers earlier in the restoration effort. However, Santa Rosa…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia River Electric Cooperative is making progress in restoring power across the region following widespread outages, with crews working around the clock to get customers back online.

As of late Sunday night, EREC reported 678 outages remaining in Escambia County, down from higher numbers earlier in the restoration effort. However, Santa Rosa County residents are facing a longer wait, with 9,444 outages still affecting customers there.

The cooperative said hundreds of lineworkers are continuing restoration efforts throughout the night. EREC also announced that its online outage map is back in service, allowing customers to track restoration progress in their areas. The map provides real-time updates on outage locations and estimated restoration times.

Escambia County Fire Rescue responded Saturday to a residence on Sonoma Lane near Beulah Road after neighbors reported smoke coming from the house. Firefighters found the home heavily damaged by the blaze. A…
item.content:encoded: A house fire in the Beulah area over the weekend destroyed a home after an electrical outlet became overloaded, according to North Escambia. Escambia County Fire Rescue responded Saturday to a residence on Sonoma Lane near Beulah Road after neighbors reported smoke coming from the house. Firefighters found the home heavily damaged by the blaze. A family pet died in the fire. The cause has been attributed to an overloaded electrical outlet, which ignited shortly after power was restored to the home. No injuries to residents were reported.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Tightens Rules on Agricultural Land Clearing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County commissioners are moving to strengthen regulations governing land-clearing on agricultural properties, according to reporting from the Citizen Portal News Florida. The new rules aim to ensure that farmland and rural properties are used for their intended agricultural purposes while preventing unauthorized clearing that could harm…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County commissioners are moving to strengthen regulations governing land-clearing on agricultural properties, according to reporting from the Citizen Portal News Florida. The new rules aim to ensure that farmland and rural properties are used for their intended agricultural purposes while preventing unauthorized clearing that could harm local ecosystems.

The measure reflects growing concern among county leadership about unauthorized land disturbance in agricultural zones. By tightening oversight, officials hope to strike a balance between protecting property rights and preserving environmental quality in Santa Rosa County's rural areas.

Details about the specific regulations, timeline for implementation, and enforcement mechanisms were not immediately available. The county has not yet announced public hearing dates or provided a formal text of the proposed rule changes.

item.title: Pensacola on Day 3 of Isaias recovery; FPL targets Monday restoration
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Pensacola is entering its third day of response and recovery operations following Hurricane Isaias, with emergency crews focused on public safety, debris clearing, and restoring critical services to residents. According to a Sunday evening update from the city, Florida Power & Light is working to restore power to 95 percent of…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola is entering its third day of response and recovery operations following Hurricane Isaias, with emergency crews focused on public safety, debris clearing, and restoring critical services to residents.

According to a Sunday evening update from the city, Florida Power & Light is working to restore power to 95 percent of customers who can safely receive service by the end of Monday, October 12. The utility's aggressive timeline reflects efforts to bring normalcy back to the area after the storm.

City officials are urging residents to remain cautious as recovery continues. Downed trees, damaged power lines, and other storm hazards remain scattered throughout Pensacola and surrounding areas. Emergency responders remind the public to avoid debris piles and report any dangerous conditions to local authorities.

item.title: USPS Suspends Mail Delivery, Retail Services Across NW Florida Including Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service has temporarily halted mail delivery and retail operations across Northern Florida, including all Pensacola ZIP codes, due to Hurricane Isaias. The suspension affects multiple facilities throughout the region, from Pensacola to Panama City and surrounding areas in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and surrounding counties. According to…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service has temporarily halted mail delivery and retail operations across Northern Florida, including all Pensacola ZIP codes, due to Hurricane Isaias. The suspension affects multiple facilities throughout the region, from Pensacola to Panama City and surrounding areas in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and surrounding counties.

According to a USPS Florida 1 District announcement issued today, affected ZIP codes include all five Pensacola service areas (32501, 32502, 32503, 32504, 32506, 32507, 32508), as well as surrounding communities like Gulf Breeze, Navarre, Milton, Cantonment, and Gonzalez. The postal service said there are currently no alternate delivery or retail locations available.

The USPS said it will work to restore operations as quickly as it can safely do so. The service disruption impacts mail delivery, package handling, and retail counter services across the affected zones. Residents and businesses can check usps.com/news or the USPS Service Alerts page for updated information on when service will resume.

item.title: DOH-Escambia Closing Monday Due to Hurricane Isaias Impacts
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County will close its Fairfield location on Monday, October 12, as the region deals with severe weather from Hurricane Isaias. All DOH-Escambia offices are expected to reopen Tuesday, October 13. Residents needing health services or information during the closure can contact the State Assistance…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County will close its Fairfield location on Monday, October 12, as the region deals with severe weather from Hurricane Isaias. All DOH-Escambia offices are expected to reopen Tuesday, October 13.

Residents needing health services or information during the closure can contact the State Assistance Information Line at 800-342-3557 for emergency resources and up-to-date disaster information. For immediate medical emergencies, call 911.

Escambia County residents seeking additional severe weather resources, shelter information, and disaster preparedness guidance can visit the Florida Division of Emergency Management website at floridadisaster.org or Escambia County's emergency management page at myescambia.com/our-services/public-safety/beready.

item.title: Escambia County starts Hurricane Isaias debris pickup Wednesday

The county is accepting only storm-generated debris from the hurricane. Residents who have damage from Isaias should place their debris on the public right-of-way — typically the area between…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County will launch debris collection this week for materials left behind by Hurricane Isaias, with operations set to begin Wednesday, October 14.

The county is accepting only storm-generated debris from the hurricane. Residents who have damage from Isaias should place their debris on the public right-of-way — typically the area between their property line and the street — to prepare for pickup.

This collection effort follows the standard county protocol for post-hurricane cleanup, allowing residents to clear hurricane-damaged trees, branches, roofing materials, and other storm debris from their properties.

item.title: DOH-Escambia Reminds Residents of Boil Water Precautions After Storm
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County is urging residents to follow boil water notice guidelines until they receive official confirmation from their water service provider that tap water is safe to use again. The advisory comes in the wake of a storm that may have compromised local water supplies. Residents should boil water for at…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County is urging residents to follow boil water notice guidelines until they receive official confirmation from their water service provider that tap water is safe to use again. The advisory comes in the wake of a storm that may have compromised local water supplies.

Residents should boil water for at least one minute before drinking, cooking, making ice, or brushing teeth. Bottled water is also a safe alternative if available. The precautions help eliminate harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites that may have entered the water system during the storm.

A current list of active boil water notices by service provider is available on the Florida Department of Health website at floridahealth.gov/environmental-health/drinking-water/boil-water-notices. Residents whose provider is not listed should continue taking precautions until they receive direct notification that the water is safe.

Other safety measures include allowing boiled water to cool before use, using boiled or bottled water to wash dishes and sanitize food-contact items, and providing boiled or bottled water to pets. DOH-Escambia is working with local water utilities to monitor water quality and lift notices as soon as conditions permit. For more information, contact the State Assistance Information Line at 1-800-342-3557.
